answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybils with source-linked escalating fees: every identity that acts pays a small fee, but identities traceable to the same funding source face a fee that doubles with each extra identity in the same epoch. Like a falcon spotting one bird among a nebula of decoys, the ledger sees the shared pulse behind the swarm: one honest agent pays the base fee once, while an attacker spawning a thousand clones pays an exponentially rising total that exceeds any gain from fake votes. Clones add cost faster than influence, making large fakery irrational.
